Sara — great to get the workload sketch, thanks. Recap + quick answers below; Ben and Neha are looped for perf/playbook specifics and pilot ops.

Recap of what you shared:
- Target: p50 < 150ms / p95 < 400ms (256 tokens typical)
- Sustained 40 rps, bursts to 120 rps (30s), concurrency 350 primary / 80 secondary
- Streaming: SSE preferred on web, WebSocket for mobile

Quick answers and trade-offs:
1) Feasibility on Redwood hosted (quantized open model):
   - For 256-token sequences we regularly see p50 TTFT in the 80–180ms range on optimised kernels with prefix KV caching; p95 depends a lot on concurrency and backend packing. At your burst levels, p95 ~400ms is achievable with tuned batching and a small dedicated pool (or reserved capacity).
2) What pushes p95 higher:
   - Large batching windows (we avoid long waits by using continuous micro-batching), cold KV cache misses, and backend scheduling queuing during bursts.
3) Streaming approach (SSE vs WS) and chunk cadence:
   - SSE is fine for browsers and simpler to operate (HTTP/2-compatible).
   - We recommend sending the first chunk as soon as the model emits tokens (first chunk ideally < 20B of text) — that gives perceived TTFT advantages.
   - Chunk cadence: 120–300ms cadence is a common sweet spot for textual UIs; lower than 100ms increases overhead, higher than 400ms feels choppy.
4) Suggested pilot configuration:
   - Dedicated burst-capacity pool with autoscale to cover 120 rps bursts; initial pilot of 2x gpus with reserved KV cache.
   - Instrumentation: per-request TTFT, chunk timestamps, and prefix cache hit rate.

Next steps I suggest:
- Ben to propose a pilot MOP and a simple benchmark script (we can replay your attached XLS)
- Neha to propose a baseline SLO package and expected cost delta for dedicated vs hosted (ballpark)
- Tentative pilot start: week of Aug 17 (subject to your availability)

I attached a proposed pilot MOP and a mutual action plan for quick alignment.

Tom/Sara — quick follow-up answering infra questions and confirming next steps.

Payload size sensitivity:
- Small prompts (<= 4 KB): negligible added TTFT beyond baseline network + model startup; p95 largely driven by concurrency and cache misses.
- Medium prompts (4–20 KB): per-token compute increases; we typically see p95 shift by +30–120ms depending on batch behaviour and model decoder speed.
- Large prompts (>20 KB): more pronounced tail — recommend pre-chunking/document embeddings for long-context summarization to keep interactive TTFT tight.

Region and routing:
- Cross-region adds network RTT; US-west <-> US-east can add ~40–80ms typical RTT. That counts against your p95 budget. For sub-500ms p95 in US-east, we recommend either (a) regional routing to an east region or (b) Dedicated capacity in US-east.

SSE vs WebSocket for TTFT:
- Connection persistence (WS) saves handshake time for long-lived sessions and can reduce first-byte overhead for the first chunk when connections are reused. For browser clients opening a fresh connection per request, WS and SSE perform similarly.

Pilot ops and next steps (action items):
- Ben: will share a benchmark script and expected pilot resource sizing by EOD Friday (2026-08-06).
- Neha: will email a baseline SLO package and a high-level cost delta (hosted vs dedicated) by Mon 2026-08-09.
- Fintego: confirm pilot scope (which endpoints, which traffic percentage) and preferred start week (we proposed Aug 17).

I'll also include a short checklist in the pilot MOP for chunk cadence testing (we'll sweep cadence at 100ms/200ms/300ms/500ms and report UX metrics + cost).

If that all sounds good I'll lock in the pilot MOP and calendar invites.
